clue.text: Dealing with others' distress

indicators.note: dealing cards means shuffling them out, so the letters of the next word are mixed

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter, leaving the six letters of the plain word

explanation.surface: Someone is coping with the suffering of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealing with' reads as coping, but 'Dealing' is the shuffle signal: OTHERS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the throes of something is to be in great pain or struggle, a state of distress.

clue.text: Traps — ten possibly — set in the church

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the two words might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Traps, perhaps ten, laid inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross arms of a cruciform church are part of the building, set within it.

clue.text: Withdrew military personnel and discussed terms

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to treat is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Troops pulled back after negotiating.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to pull back, withdraw.

clue.text: To be uppity is certainly not a good thing

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Being arrogant is surely a bad trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppity' looks like arrogance, but in a down entry it signals LIVE written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness is the opposite of good.

clue.text: Just the same, a lot of people will be present

parts.note: 'do' is short for ditto, meaning the same as above
a nation is a large body of people

explanation.surface: An observation that, all the same, a crowd will turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray 'pie' that the printed page does not show. 'present' reads as attending, but it is a noun: a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, something given as a present.

clue.text: Cow needing some cover — a weatherproof shelter

indicators.note: some of the following words' letters give the answer, running across them

explanation.surface: A cow wants a little roof over it, a rainproof shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal, but it is a verb: to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, to fill them with awe.

clue.text: Gain a stone maybe. Contend with that!

indicators.note: maybe signals these letters may be arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Putting on weight, then having to cope with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text broke 'Contend' with a line-end hyphen. 'Gain a stone' reads as weight gain; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke hostility in someone is to set yourself in conflict with them.

clue.text: One's allowed to see this little place

parts.note: one is I, and I's is short for I is
let means permitted, allowed

explanation.surface: A person is permitted to visit a small spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a tiny bit of land, a little place.

clue.text: Registering no sound

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound

explanation.surface: A meter recording silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing and recording something is registering it.

clue.text: A fat goat?

explanation.surface: A question whether a goat is overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: A goat butts, so it is a 'butter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy spread is a fat; one that rams with its head, as a goat does, butts.

clue.text: A feature of credit

explanation.surface: A note that something is a characteristic of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a quality or characteristic; to attribute something is to credit it to someone.

clue.text: Vacant though sober man receiving approval in Spain -

indicators.note: the sober man takes in the approval, so those letters go inside

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a man who does not drink
ole is the Spanish cry of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: An empty house, despite a teetotaller being cheered in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A property advertised as available for rent stands empty, unoccupied.

clue.text: Hold back support

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrain one's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check it; a stem is the stalk that holds up a flower.

clue.text: Tear things out and arrange in order

indicators.note: letters turned out of their places are rearranged, so the two words before are shuffled

explanation.surface: Instructions to rip items out and then sort them tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'tear out', but it signals the rearrangement of TEAR THINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy something up is to put it right, set it straight.

clue.text: Old driver creating a commotion in high spirits

indicators.note: the commotion goes inside the high spirits

parts.note: cheer is gladness, high spirits
a riot is a commotion

explanation.surface: An ancient chauffeur causing a disturbance while merry.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver of a horse-drawn war carriage in the ancient world.

clue.text: Vessel on which one's likely to suffer mal-de-mer?

definitions.text: on which one's likely to suffer mal-de-mer?

explanation.surface: A boat that makes passengers seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship that pitches in a heavy sea makes people sick, so it is a 'pitcher'; mal-de-mer is French for seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug for pouring is a vessel; a ship that rises and falls bow to stern pitches, causing seasickness.

clue.text: He's given a home by Her Majesty

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A man housed by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a man's name. ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so a fair stand-in for an unnamed man.

clue.text: A player's entitlement

parts.note: an actor's title, the name they perform under rather than their own

explanation.surface: What a sportsman is due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests sport and 'entitlement' a right, but the player is an actor and the entitlement a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's professional name is what they are called on the boards.

clue.text: The man despised for leaving dry land with a certain hesitation

parts.note: a desert is arid land
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A man hated for quitting an arid place with some faltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons his post or cause is scorned for going.

clue.text: Greatly admires revolutionary leader in a works

indicators.note: the leading letter goes inside the phrase that follows, 'a works'

parts.note: does means works, as in performs

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone worships a revolutionary figurehead within a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a works' looks like a factory, but it is A plus DOES; R, the first letter of 'revolutionary', goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love or worship them deeply.

clue.text: Give voice about fuel causing pollution

indicators.note: the singing goes round the fuel, holding it inside

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Speaking out on fuel that causes pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtying something is making it filthy, polluting it.

clue.text: Writers must pay the price

parts.note: letter writers have to pay the cost of sending what they post

explanation.surface: Authors have to face the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay the price' reads as suffering consequences; here it is the literal fee for sending a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge for sending mail is what correspondents pay to the post office.

clue.text: Spoke at length and quietly administered a reproof

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to rate someone is an old verb for scolding

explanation.surface: Someone talked on and then softly scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate' here is an old verb meaning to scold, not to value.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk on and on, foolishly, is to babble or chatter.

clue.text: Points heavenward

parts.note: tapering church towers that point up to the sky

explanation.definitionFit: Tall tapering church structures aim at the sky.

clue.text: Occasional police raid may be ordered

indicators.note: the letters can be put into a new order, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police raid might be called now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine published at intervals, or something recurring now and then, is occasional.

clue.text: The way to beat the egg head

parts.note: to rout is to defeat heavily

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for whisking an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat the egg' reads as cookery; 'beat' is ROUT and 'egg head' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or course is the way to go.

clue.text: A server of drinks entered in the beauty contest

indicators.note: the answer has been entered inside the next words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A barmaid takes part in a beauty pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hebe was cupbearer to the gods, serving their nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe poured nectar for the Olympian gods, a cupbearer in myth.

clue.text: Deal arranged by a Spartan Queen

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the word deal are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A bargain fixed by a queen of Sparta.
explanation.walkthrough: Leda was queen of Sparta in Greek myth, visited by Zeus as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was wife of Tyndareus, king of Sparta.

clue.text: Disturb with sound arguments

indicators.note: sound here means said aloud, so the word for arguments is heard as another

parts.note: rows are quarrels, arguments

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by well-reasoned points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound arguments' reads as good reasoning, but 'sound' signals that ROWS (rhymes with 'cows') is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake or stir someone up is to disturb them.

clue.text: New line offered by cunning agent lacking polish

indicators.note: a new version of the word line is a rearranged one
cunning suggests the word agent is twisted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A spy comes up with a crude chat-up line.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'New' turns LINE into INEL, and 'cunning' turns AGENT into EGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clumsy or graceless lacks refinement.

clue.text: Neat article for example backing cheap way to travel

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and a steer is a bullock
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation goes backwards

explanation.surface: A tidy grammatical item supporting budget travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' means cattle, not tidy; EG reverses to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-priced passenger class on a ship was the cheapest accommodation.

clue.text: Run personal transport — always short!

parts.note: a car is one's own vehicle

indicators.note: short means contracted, as in the poetic form missing a letter

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: An exhortation to drive a car, always briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' signals the poetic contraction e'er for EVER, dropping the V.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong, to run at speed.
